sub_areas.name: Downtown Hamilton (lower city)
sub_areas.note: Central Hamilton extends from the base of the Mountain north to Barton Street, west to Chedoke Creek or Dundurn Street, and east to about Wentworth Street or Sherman Avenue (Wikipedia, Geography of Hamilton). OGS point queries at the reference coordinate (43.25011, -79.84963) and at Hamilton GO Centre (43.25306, -79.86917) both return unit 9 coarse-textured glaciolacustrine deposits (sand, gravel, minor silt and clay) over Queenston Formation red shale; the Dundurn Castle point (43.26948, -79.88465) returns unit 9b littoral deposits over Queenston.

sub_areas.name: Hamilton Mountain
sub_areas.note: The Niagara Escarpment bisects the city into 'upper' and 'lower' parts; the Hamilton portion is in many places 100 m tall and is locally called 'the Mountain' (Wikipedia, Geography of Hamilton). OGS point queries at Lime Ridge Mall (43.218, -79.862) and Mohawk College (43.23822, -79.88569) return unit 8a fine-textured glaciolacustrine deposits (silt and clay, minor sand and gravel; massive to well laminated) over Lockport Formation dolostone (Silurian).

sub_areas.name: Ancaster
sub_areas.note: Former town, amalgamated into the City of Hamilton in 2001 (Wikipedia). OGS point query at the Wikipedia article coordinate (43.22556, -79.97667) returns unit 9 coarse-textured glaciolacustrine deposits (sand, gravel, minor silt and clay) over Lockport Formation dolostone (Silurian); this is above the escarpment, so the bedrock is dolostone, not Queenston shale.

sub_areas.name: Dundas
sub_areas.note: 'Valley Town', at the bottom of the Niagara Escarpment on the western edge of Lake Ontario, bounded by the Dundas Valley Conservation Area (Wikipedia). OGS point query at (43.26611, -79.95472) returns unit 12 older alluvial deposits (clay, silt, sand, gravel, may contain organic remains) over Queenston Formation red shale.

sub_areas.name: Stoney Creek
sub_areas.note: Community 10 km east of downtown on the south shore of western Lake Ontario, fed by Stoney Creek and other minor streams; the historic 'Old Town' is below the escarpment and the lower city grew mainly in the 1970s and 1980s (Wikipedia). OGS point query at (43.2164, -79.755) returns unit 5d clay-to-silt-textured till (derived from glaciolacustrine deposits or shale) over Queenston Formation red shale.

sub_areas.name: Waterdown / Flamborough
sub_areas.note: Waterdown OGS point query at the Wikipedia coordinate (43.33333, -79.88333) returns unit 5d clay-to-silt-textured till over Amabel Formation dolostone (Silurian). Rural Flamborough points: (43.346, -80.055) returns unit 5b stone-poor sandy silt to silty sand till over Guelph Formation dolostone; Carlisle (43.401, -79.9755) returns unit 6 ice-contact stratified deposits (sand and gravel, minor silt, clay and till) over Amabel Formation dolostone.

sub_areas.name: Glanbrook / Binbrook / Mount Hope
sub_areas.note: Binbrook is in southeastern Hamilton, amalgamated with Mount Hope to form Glanbrook in 1974 and into the City of Hamilton in 2001; population 10,791 (2021) (Wikipedia). OGS point queries at Binbrook (43.1217, -79.8045), the Glanbrook article coordinate (43.178, -79.932) and the Hamilton airport at Mount Hope (43.17361, -79.935) all return unit 8a fine-textured glaciolacustrine silt and clay over Guelph Formation dolostone (Silurian).

sub_areas.name: Westdale / McMaster (west lower city)
sub_areas.note: OGS point query at McMaster University (43.26333, -79.91889) returns unit 9 coarse-textured glaciolacustrine sand and gravel over Queenston Formation red shale.

sub_areas.name: Red Hill Valley (east lower city)
sub_areas.note: Red Hill Creek is one of the creeks that flow over the escarpment within city limits (Wikipedia, Geography of Hamilton). OGS point query at the Red Hill Valley article coordinate (43.2234, -79.7981) returns unit 5d clay-to-silt-textured till over Queenston Formation red shale.

surficial.unit: OGS MRD128-REV unit 9 / 9b - Coarse-textured glaciolacustrine deposits
surficial.description: Sand, gravel, minor silt and clay (unit 9); 9b is the littoral (shoreline) sub-unit. Former glacial Lake Iroquois nearshore deposits: Wikipedia records that Lake Iroquois laid down glaciolacustrine sand and clay in the lower city.
surficial.where: Lower city and Ancaster: query points at the reference coordinate (43.25011, -79.84963), Hamilton GO Centre, McMaster/Westdale and Ancaster return unit 9; Dundurn Castle returns 9b.

surficial.description: Silt and clay, minor sand and gravel; massive to well laminated.
surficial.where: Above the escarpment on the Mountain and across Glanbrook: query points at Lime Ridge Mall, Mohawk College, Binbrook, the Glanbrook coordinate and the Hamilton airport (Mount Hope) all return unit 8a.

bedrock.formation: Queenston Formation (Upper Ordovician red shale) below the escarpment; Lockport Formation, Amabel Formation and Guelph Formation dolostones (Silurian) above it (OGS MRD219).
bedrock.description: Queenston: red shale and siltstone, minor green shale and siltstone, and variable calcareous siltstone to sandstone and limestone interbeds; returned at the reference coordinate, Hamilton GO Centre, Dundurn Castle, McMaster, Dundas, Stoney Creek and Red Hill Valley. Lockport: thick-bedded blue-grey crinoidal limestone to dolostone (Gasport Mb), cherty dolostone (Goat Island Mb), argillaceous dolostone and shale (Vinemount shale beds) and bituminous dark brown dolostone (Eramosa Mb); returned at Ancaster, Lime Ridge Mall and Mohawk College. Amabel: white to blue-grey thick- to massive-bedded dolostone; returned at Waterdown and Carlisle. Guelph: tan to brown sucrosic fossiliferous dolostone; returned at Binbrook, Glanbrook, Mount Hope airport and rural Flamborough. Wikipedia describes the Hamilton escarpment as a wall of limestone, sandstone and shale, with Ordovician shale and sandstone at the base and Silurian limestone and dolomite beds at the top.
bedrock.depth_note: Depth to bedrock was not retrieved (no drift-thickness dataset queried). None of the 16 OGS surficial point queries in Hamilton returned unit 3 (bedrock at or near surface), unlike Oakville; every point returned a mapped drift unit of unstated thickness. The escarpment face itself, which Wikipedia puts at about 100 m tall in many places, is exposed rock.

implications_for_piles: The City of Hamilton's Residential Decks/Porches checklist lists 'Helical Pier Engineer approved specifications' and 'Ministers Ruling or BMEC Approvals for innovative materials or systems' as additional documentation to submit with a deck permit application, so a helical pile deck in Hamilton needs engineer-approved pile specifications in the application package.

The City's sample wood deck drawing sets the conventional baseline: piers (example 10 in. diameter sono tube belled to 14 in.) drawn to 'MIN. 48"' below grade, with the note that materials other than lumber require engineered specifications, and that no attachment is permitted to or through brick veneer, so piers must support the deck at the house on brick-veneer homes.

Soil changes with the escarpment: OGS maps sand and gravel (unit 9) under the lower city and Ancaster, laminated silt and clay (unit 8a) across the Mountain and Glanbrook, and clay-silt till (5d) at Stoney Creek, Red Hill and Waterdown; an engineer's pile depth and torque determination for one of these is not transferable to the others.

Bedrock also changes with the escarpment: Queenston red shale below it, Lockport/Amabel/Guelph dolostone above it; where drift is thin the refusal material differs (shale versus hard dolostone). No site-specific drift thickness, torque or capacity figures were retrieved.

permits.authority: City of Hamilton Building Division (Planning and Economic Development Department), City Hall 3rd Floor, 71 Main Street West; 905-546-2720 / 905-546-2424
permits.deck_permit_required_when: Per the City's Porches and Decks page: any-sized deck or porch (covered or uncovered) attached to a building; a detached uncovered deck or porch greater than 10 sq.m. and more than 200 mm above adjacent grade; a detached covered deck or porch greater than 10 sq.m. regardless of height; a detached deck or porch of 10 sq.m. or less that is adjacent to or associated with a door to the building and more than 600 mm above adjacent grade; and replacement or installation of new guards (railings). Decks used with a swimming pool also require a permit.
permits.footing_depth_requirement: City sample wood deck drawing (elevation views): piers drawn to 'MIN. 48"' below grade, example '10" DIAM SONO TUBE BELL TO 14"'; 'IF MATERIAL OTHER THAN LUMBER IS BEING USED, PROVIDE THE ENGINEERED SPECIFICATIONS'; 'NO ATTACHMENT PERMITTED TO OR THROUGH BRICK VENEER, PIERS WILL BE REQUIRED TO SUPPORT THE DECK AT THE HOUSE'. The Residential Decks/Porches checklist requires drawings to 'Show depth and size of piers below grade' and lists 'Helical Pier Engineer approved specifications' and 'Ministers Ruling or BMEC Approvals for innovative materials or systems' as additional documentation. No numeric soil bearing value is printed on the Hamilton drawing.
inspections: Pre-construction on-site meeting (prior to commencement of construction)
Footing Inspection (prior to pouring footings: formwork and reinforcing for footings, column pads, and structural slabs-on-grade)
Structural Inspections (when all framing has been completed and prior to any insulation being installed)

Note: the City's Building Inspections page lists these as general residential stages; it does not publish a deck-specific list. Requests are completed within 2 business days per the Ontario Building Code; book at 905-546-2424 ext. 7777 or online via my.hamilton.ca for permits issued after July 6, 2026.
permits.fee_note: Building By-law 15-058, Schedule A (as posted on the City's Building Permit Fees page on 2026-09-25 and in the office consolidation dated January 31, 2025, latest amendment By-law 25-008): 'Deck, balcony, open porch, stairs' Service Index $5.36 per m2 of floor area, subject to the minimum permit fee of $291; fees are rounded to the nearest dollar, are subject to HST where applicable, and must be paid when the application is submitted. Derived example: a 20 m2 deck computes to $107, so the $291 minimum applies. No separately labelled '2026 fee schedule' document was found; the page carries no effective-date line, so the 2026 currency of these figures is inferred from the page being live on 2026-09-25.
permits.timeline_note: No fixed permit-review day count is published on the City's Porches and Decks, Application Requirements or Review and Approval pages; staff contact the applicant when the application is approved or incomplete. Inspection requests are completed within 2 business days as per the Ontario Building Code (City Building Inspections page).
permits.portal_note: Applications are submitted online by the owner or an agent: create a my.hamilton.ca account, then select the Building Permits category to create a Customer Portal account, then Getting Started > Permitting & Inspections. Submissions must be vector PDFs, unsecured, black and white, drawn to scale, and follow By-law 15-058 drawing requirements.
